newsitem.title: USA: US refiners gobble up foreign crude as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: US refiners gobble up foreign crude as prices rise.

text.p: U.S. refiners along the Gulf Coast were seen gobbling up foreign crudes on Friday amid steadily increasing prices, traders said.
A cargo of North Sea benchmark Brent crude for early June arrival was on offer at 55 cents a barrel under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
More Brent was available for mid-June at WTI/Cushing minus 60 cents a barrel.
Earlier this week, the bellwether grade was assessed at a weaker WTI minus 70-75 cents a barrel.
"Excellent demand in Europe and the Far East" has soaked up much of the foreign crude from the North Sea and West Africa, a Texas trader said.
Earlier this week, Norwegian Oseberg for mid-May arrival was placed around WTI minus 85 cents a barrel.
Heidrun for June 1-5 delivery traded around WTI minus $1.80 a barrel, while Troll for the same dates moved at WTI minus 60 cents a barrel.
Oseberg for mid-June was on offer at WTI minus 50 cents a barrel, traders said.

The spread between WTI and Brent narrowed to around $1.55-65 a barrel Friday afternoon. Dated Brent activity was thin, although dated barrels were assessed at a firm June Brent minus 20 cents, traders said.
From West Africa, a European company was offering Nigerian Bonny Light into the Louisiana Offshore Oil Port (LOOP) for end-May around June WTI minus 17 cents.
Brass River for early June was on offer at dated Brent plus $1.95 a barrel.
In Latin America, prices have also firmed not only as a result of healthier demand but also because of dramatically lower freight rates in the Caribbean.
Colombian Cusiana was last done around WTI minus $1.25 a barrel, confirming the grade's new stronger price range.
Colombia's state Ecopetrol was tendering a Vasconia cargo for June 23-30 loading, traders said.
Venezuelan Furrial was last placed around WTI minus $3.25 a barrel, up from a $3.45-level a few days ago, traders said.
Ecuadoran Oriente for delivery around July 10 was pegged around WTI minus $3.35 a barrel.
From Argentina, 950,000 barrels of Canadon Seco was on offer for June 16-17 fob mother vessel, traders said.
